title: KV cache hit-rate experiments (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick iterative lab notes while tuning prefix/KV cache sharding and eviction heuristics. Trying to reproduce weird p50 jitter on tail workloads and understand how hit-rate correlates with observed token CPU/GPU time and overall requester latency.

Test context (short):
- Runtime: local dev cluster (dedicated-dev pool), 4x A100s, nfvi build: v2.14.1-experimental
- Model: redwood-3B-v1 (float16), kv-cache enabled in runtime
- Inference config: temperature=0.0, max_new_tokens=128, stop=None (streaming disabled for bench)
- Workloads: short-chat (avg prompt tokens=60), long-chat (avg prompt tokens=1024), prefix-heavy (repeated system prompt across many requests)
- Measurement: request wall-time (client-observed), server-side per-token CPU and GPU ms (from profiler), kv cache hit-rate sampled by request

Experiment matrix (high level):
- cache_shards: [1, 4, 8]
- local_cache_size_per_shard (entries): [512, 2048]
- eviction_policy: [LRU, TTL-1m]
- batch_target: [1, 4, 16]

Run logs (select runs). Each line: run-id | params | workload | observed hit% | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | notes

R-20250218-01 | shards=1 size=512 evict=LRU bt=4 | short-chat | hit=21% | p50=78 | p95=220 | tiny hit-rate, high p95, CPU dominated (KV misses show redispatch to full forward)
R-20250218-02 | shards=4 size=512 evict=LRU bt=4 | short-chat | hit=63% | p50=42 | p95=110 | large improvement, mem-locality increase, but some cross-shard locking stalls seen in trace
R-20250218-03 | shards=8 size=512 evict=LRU bt=4 | short-chat | hit=68% | p50=39 | p95=95  | marginal hit-rate gain vs shards=4, but scheduling jitter up a bit (thread contention on cache mutexes)
R-20250218-04 | shards=4 size=2048 evict=LRU bt=4 | prefix-heavy | hit=92% | p50=31 | p95=70 | best for prefix-heavy, almost all tokens served from KV, small GPU load
R-20250218-05 | shards=4 size=2048 evict=TTL-1m bt=4 | prefix-heavy | hit=88% | p50=33 | p95=78 | TTL evict slightly worse here (working set fits) but safer for memory
R-20250218-06 | shards=4 size=512 evict=LRU bt=16 | short-chat | hit=60% | p50=48 | p95=135 | batching improved throughput but increased p95 due to queueing when bursty
R-20250219-01 | shards=4 size=512 evict=LRU bt=1 | long-chat  | hit=12% | p50=300 | p95=720 | long contexts cause KV miss because we only cache last N tokens; need re-evaluate prefix segmentation
R-20250219-03 | shards=4 size=2048 evict=LRU bt=1 | long-chat  | hit=35% | p50=210 | p95=490 | improved but still heavy compute on long tails

Quick observations:
- Hit-rate correlates strongly with p50 and p95 for short-chat/prefix-heavy (obvious), but for long-chat the placement of cached segments matters more than absolute cache size (we store only last 1024 keys per request).
- Sharding from 1 -> 4 gives biggest win for local lock contention and CPU/GPU pipeline utilization. 8 shards shows diminishing returns and introduces more locking overhead in our current implementation.
- Larger per-shard cache (2048) helps prefix-heavy workloads dramatically; cost is memory and slightly increased lookup latency (but net win).
- Eviction TTL is safer for multi-tenant but LRU performs better when working sets are stable.
- High batching helps throughput across the board, but for bursty interactive traffic it increased tail latencies due to queueing. There's a trade-off vs latency SLOs.

Mini table (aggregated):
| config | workload | hit% | p50 | p95 | notes |
| shards=4,size=512,bt=4 | short-chat | 63 | 42 | 110 | good baseline |
| shards=4,size=2048,bt=4 | prefix-heavy | 92 | 31 | 70 | best for repeated prompts |
| shards=4,size=512,bt=1 | long-chat | 12 | 300 | 720 | misses on long context |

Profiler snippets (copied):
- KV lookup cost per token (miss): ~0.35ms CPU + 1.6ms GPU work for full forward
- KV lookup cost per token (hit): ~0.05ms CPU + 0.2ms GPU memory ops
- Cross-shard lock wait (8 shards): median=0.12ms, p99=5.8ms (explains jitter)

Open questions & hypotheses:
- Are we doing unnecessary full forward recomputation on partial prefix misses? (todo: inspect code path tracer INF-874)
- Could an adaptive eviction policy (freq-based aging) give better hit/size tradeoff for long-chat?
- Is cross-shard lock contention due to a single mutex per-shard or due to our instrumentation sampling? Need micro-traces at 50us granularity.

Action items (next runs):
- A1: run adaptive-evict simulation locally (script: bench/kv/adaptive_v1) with long-chat workload, record hit % and p95 (owner: me)
- A2: instrument per-shard mutex hold times and try replacing one mutex with RW-lock in a dev build (owner: Evan)
- A3: test smaller batch_target=2 for interactive flows and compare p95 under Poisson arrival (spike emulation)

Notes to self:
- Keep small reproducible dataset for prefix-heavy scenario (example prompts in /tmp/kv-bench/prefix-set.json).
- Link to trace snapshots: CONFLUENCE-TRACE-551 (TODO: upload full traces)
- Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1423 (kv sharding refactor)

Rough conclusion: for now, default to shards=4 and cache_size=2048 for customers whose workloads are prefix-heavy or chat with many repeated prompts. For long-context customers, investigate segment-aware caching (store longer-term prefix segments keyed by prompt fingerprint).

Random scribbles: TTL=90s option looked promising for multi-tenant fairness but hurts hit% when working set stable. Consider hybrid (LRU + tenant quotas).

References/linked artifacts: see linked_artifacts field for quick links.

-- olivia
(more to run, will iterate)
